items.key: 11.32.0 :: New Features and Enhancements > Platform APIs and Platform API Gateway General Availability
items.title: New Features and Enhancements > Platform APIs and Platform API Gateway General Availability — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
Platform APIs provide access to device management, compliance, blueprints, declaration reporting, and actions across the Jamf platform through a single endpoint surface. They replace fragmented, product-specific workflows with a standardized foundation for building automations and integrations for Apple at enterprise scale. You can access Platform APIs through the Platform API Gateway.
The Platform API Gateway provides a common endpoint structure and a single authentication model for accessing Platform APIs and product APIs across the Jamf platform. Credentials are managed centrally in Jamf Account, with least-privilege scoping and multiple scope levels to match different integration and automation needs.
For more information on accessing the Jamf Pro API through the Platform API Gateway, see Getting started in the Platform API Reference. If you have an existing integration built against the Jamf Pro API or Classic API, Jamf recommends migrating it to the Platform API Gateway. For information, see Move an existing integration to the Platform API Gateway in the Platform API Reference.
Note:
Jamf recommends accessing the Jamf Pro API through the Platform API Gateway. However, you can continue accessing the Jamf Pro API and Classic API without using the Platform API Gateway.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: New Features and Enhancements > UUID Column for Advanced Searches
items.title: New Features and Enhancements > UUID Column for Advanced Searches — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
A UUID column can be enabled for searches on the Scope and Criteria pages, including smart group criteria. The UUID column provides a static identifier that you can use to ensure you are selecting the correct group, even if you have groups with identical names.
This column is hidden by default. To display it, navigate to Account settings > Interface Preferences and select Show UUID column in group searches. Deselect the checkbox to hide the column again.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: New Features and Enhancements > Active Users Display
items.title: New Features and Enhancements > Active Users Display — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
Note:
This change was introduced in Jamf Pro 11.29.0 (June 2026) and was inadvertently omitted from those release notes.
The Jamf Pro navigation header can now display all logged-in users, providing administrators with a comprehensive view of active users in their instance. Up to five active users are displayed at a time, each represented by a circular avatar with the user's initials. You can also hold the pointer over a user to see their active session duration. The display refreshes every 30 seconds to keep the view current.
To enable this feature, navigate to Settings > System > Active users display.
Note:
Administrators with full privileges can view all active users, regardless of site.
Site administrators can only view active users in their assigned site.
Administrators with custom privileges require Read access to the "Users" privilege to view active users.
If an administrator has multiple sessions open simultaneously, only the oldest session is displayed.
Active users are not displayed when accessing Jamf Pro via a mobile device.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: New Features and Enhancements > Other Changes and Improvements
items.title: New Features and Enhancements > Other Changes and Improvements — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
The workflow options for Simplified Setup for Platform Single Sign-on have been renamed for clarity. Attended is now Identity first, and Unattended is now Device first. Both workflows retain their current behavior, and existing configurations require no changes.
Managed computers now validate packages hosted on the Jamf Cloud Distribution Service (JCDS) with SHA-256 hashes before installation, replacing MD5 and SHA3-512. This change requires no configuration. Packages hosted on file share, Akamai NetStorage, Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront, or Rackspace distribution points are not affected and continue to use their existing hash algorithms.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: New Features and Enhancements > Further Considerations
items.title: New Features and Enhancements > Further Considerations — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
See the latest Jamf Pro Release Notes Video for a brief overview of new features and enhancements.
Known issues for Jamf Pro can be accessed from the Jamf Account portal.
For non-administrator Jamf Pro user accounts, privileges associated with new features in Jamf Pro are disabled by default. If you have Custom privilege configurations for user accounts or groups in your environment, a Jamf Pro user account with Administrator privileges must manually enable new feature privileges for each user or group with Custom privileges.
Jamf recommends clearing your browser's cache after upgrading Jamf Pro to ensure that the Jamf Pro interface displays correctly.
See the Jamf Pro API Changelog for a list of new, deprecated, and removed endpoints.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: Important Notices > Changes to Microsoft's Baseline Scope Enforcement for Device Compliance with Jamf Pro
items.title: Important Notices > Changes to Microsoft's Baseline Scope Enforcement for Device Compliance with Jamf Pro — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
If your organization uses the Jamf device compliance integration, it may have recently been impacted by the change to baseline scope enforcement, described in the following Microsoft documentation:
Improved enforcement for All resources policies with resource exclusions
Jamf has recently updated the macOS device compliance registration flow to allow organizations to exclude it from Conditional Access policies. For instructions on configuring your environment to do this, see the Configuring Jamf Pro Device Compliance for Microsoft's Baseline Scope Enforcement article. After completing these steps, if you previously made temporary changes as described in the Device Compliance Registration Blocked by Conditional Access Policies article, you can safely revert those changes.
Important:
Due to a known issue (PI-1580), this new configuration does not yet support Conditional Access policies that require user interaction (such as multifactor authentication). If you cannot exclude the user registration app from policies requiring user interaction, do not follow the above instructions yet. Jamf is actively working on a fix for this issue. Contact Jamf Support for more information.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: Important Notices > OS 27 Software Update Deprecations and Affected Jamf Pro Features
items.title: Important Notices > OS 27 Software Update Deprecations and Affected Jamf Pro Features — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
At WWDC 2025, Apple deprecated MDM software update commands as part of the shift to declarative device management for OS update management. Because these legacy mechanisms are deprecated at the protocol level, every functionality that leverages them is also deprecated, regardless of the source product or vendor. Any workflow, smart group, or automation dependent on these mechanisms will fail silently or return stale data. For more information, see the following documentation from Apple:

Jamf recommends you update any workflow in your environment that relies on legacy mechanisms prior to the OS 27 release.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: Important Notices > Upcoming New Privileges for Mass Actions
items.title: Important Notices > Upcoming New Privileges for Mass Actions — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
In an upcoming release, new privileges for mass actions will be added to Jamf Pro:
Send Mass Lock Command for Computers
Send Mass Wipe Command for Computers
Send Mass Unmanage Command for Computers
Mass Delete Computer Inventory Records
Send Mass Lock Command for Mobile Devices
Send Mass Wipe Command for Mobile Devices
Send Mass Unmanage Command for Mobile Devices
Mass Delete Mobile Device Inventory Records
Previously, performing any of these mass actions only required the corresponding privilege for a single device. This change will limit high-impact actions to the administrators and API clients that require them. These privileges will not be added to any existing account automatically, and they will not be included in the "Administrator" privilege set. If your organization needs an account or API client to perform these actions, you will need to create or update a custom privilege set and explicitly grant the privileges.
To prepare for this change, Jamf recommends you review any accounts and API clients that currently perform mass lock, wipe, unmanage, or delete actions on computers or mobile devices, and plan to grant the new privileges through a custom privilege set once the release is available.

items.key: 11.32.0 :: Important Notices > Notice History by Release
items.title: Important Notices > Notice History by Release — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
Starting with version...Change or ConsiderationDescription
11.31.0
Self Service+ for Mobile Release
Self Service+ for mobile was released 20 July 2026 on the App Store for Apple devices. Devices with iOS or iPadOS 16.x or earlier will remain on Self Service 11.4.2.
Self Service+ for mobile expands on the Self Service experience when you create and deploy an activation profile using Jamf Security Cloud, enabling network security monitoring, threat alerts, and centralized notifications in addition to the Self Service capabilities that Jamf Pro enables.
For more information, including deployment instructions and requirements, see the Self Service+ for Mobile Deployment Guide.
11.29.0
macOS Version Reporting Inconsistency
A known issue in Jamf Pro causes a computer's macOS version to be reported inconsistently, affecting smart group and advanced search membership. The macOS version could be reported as a two-part version (e.g., 13.3) or a three-part version (e.g., 13.3.0), depending on the source of the inventory data. This inconsistency can cause computers to be temporarily added or removed from smart groups and advanced searches unexpectedly.
Jamf Pro 11.31.0 now reports the macOS version consistently as a two-part version when patch versions are not expressed in the version reported from macOS (e.g., 13.3). Jamf Pro will continue to correctly report three-part patch versions as expected.

items.title: Deprecations and Removals — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
Deprecations Added in a Previous Release
DeprecationNotes
Non-OIDC-based administrator authentication methods for cloud-hosted Jamf Pro instances
In a future release of Jamf Pro (estimated target: the second half of 2027), support for the following legacy administrator authentication methods will be removed:
Local Jamf Pro accounts
SAML-based authentication (including failover login URLs)
LDAP and directory service-based authentication
After the removal, Jamf Pro will require an OIDC-based authentication method to log in, such as Jamf ID or federation through an OIDC-compliant identity provider.
Migrating to platform authentication improves the security of your Jamf Pro environment while enabling additional platform functionality. It also ensures readiness for Apple's upcoming removal of legacy MDM software update commands by enabling the declarative device management capabilities in blueprints.
Jamf recommends migrating to a supported authentication method as soon as possible. For more information or assistance with migrating, contact your Account team.
Note:
This deprecation specifically applies to administrator login for cloud-hosted Jamf Pro instances. Self-hosted instances will not be affected.
Jamf plans to introduce replacement options for fallback access functionality in Jamf Pro before failover URLs are removed.
DigiCert PKI Platform 8 support
DigiCert PKI Platform 8 (mPKI8) end of issuance was 01 October 2025. Jamf Pro is undergoing a phased approach to this deprecation. The ability to create new mPKI8 integrations is removed. In a future release of Jamf Pro, all mPKI8 integrations and associated information (e.g., certificate deployment records) will be removed from the Jamf Pro database.
For more information on the end of issuance, see the following documentation from DigiCert:
Transitioning certificate issuance from PKI Platform 8 to DigiCert® ONE
Rackspace and Akamai cloud distribution point support
Support for distribution points hosted in Rackspace or Akamai Cloud will be removed in a future release of Jamf Pro. If your environment uses a distribution point hosted by either of these providers, Jamf recommends migrating your content to a different hosting solution, such as the Jamf Cloud Distribution Service (JCDS). Contact Jamf Support for additional information.
Self Service classic for macOS support
Self Service classic for macOS is deprecated as of 31 March 2026, meaning it will no longer receive new features or bug fixes but remains available for use. Administrators are advised to migrate to Self Service+, the new end user application, which provides the same core functionality as Self Service classic while enabling new integrations with other Jamf applications such as Jamf Connect.
Note:
While Self Service classic will no longer receive updates or bug fixes, it will continue to be deployed to computers that are unable to run Self Service+, such as those running versions earlier than macOS 13. Self Service classic continues to be available via automatic deployment if Use Self Service+ as the default end user application is not enabled. All options related to Self Service classic will continue to be available in Jamf Pro, but they will no longer be maintained.
Software identification (SWID) tags
The functionality to use software identification (SWID) tags for licensed software records will be removed.
Maintenance pages
Computer inventory collection for fonts
Estimated removal date: October 2026.
Functionality to make policies available offline
This option, currently available only for policies set to the "Ongoing" frequency, will be removed from the Jamf Pro interface, and all policies will require a connection to the Jamf Pro server to check for triggers before running.
Sign QuickAdd Package functionality for user-initiated enrollment settings
This functionality is only used in legacy enrollment workflows involving QuickAdd packages and does not affect the user-initiated enrollment workflow. Estimated removal date: November 2026.
Azure AD Graph for Conditional Access
Azure AD Graph is deprecated. If you previously modified the conditionalAccessDomains.json file, Jamf recommends editing the file to add the "msGraphResourceUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/" property into GLOBAL settings and "msGraphResourceUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.us/" into US_GOVERNMENT settings. For more information on this deprecation, see the following documentation from Microsoft:
Migrate your apps from Azure AD Graph to Microsoft Graph
Cache name setting
This setting will be removed from the Single Sign-On Extensions payload in computer and mobile device configuration profiles because Apple deprecated them.
Password expiration and Replication time settings
These settings will be removed from the Single Sign-On Extensions payload in computer configuration profiles because Apple deprecated them.
Skip Display Tone and Skip Home button sensitivity settings
These settings will be removed from the Skip Setup Items payload for mobile device configuration profiles.
Home Button Sensitivity and True Tone Display settings
These settings will be removed from the General payload for computer and mobile device PreStage enrollments.
Functionality to issue the Tomcat SSL/TLS certificate from Jamf Pro's built-in certificate authority
Jamf Pro's functionality to issue the Tomcat SSL/TLS certificate from the JSS built-in certificate authority (CA) will be discontinued. The release version for this change has not been determined. Before this change occurs, it is recommended that all on-premise Jamf Pro instances leveraging this functionality switch to a publicly trusted third-party CA to issue the Tomcat SSL/TLS certificate. This will prevent the potential loss of MDM communication from Jamf Pro to enrolled devices. If needed, a Tomcat SSL/TLS server certificate for Jamf Pro may be issued from an internal certificate authority. The JSS built-in CA will maintain its current ability to manually issue server certificates to other servers.
The "DIGEST-MD5" authentication type option
"DIGEST-MD5" will be removed from the authentication type options. This authentication type option displays when configuring an LDAP server to use Jamf Infrastructure Manager as a proxy server.
Computer Access Only and Mobile Device Access Only Limited Access settings
Jamf Pro web app instances with one of these settings configured will automatically be updated to the Computer and Mobile Device Access setting. Administrators will only be able to assign Full Access or Computer and Mobile Device Access privileges after the deprecation.
Webhook responses for ComputerPolicyFinished and ComputerCheckIn
These webhook responses will be modified to include additional information. These changes may break integrations that currently utilize these event types.
Supervise Devices and Make MDM Profile Mandatory settings in a mobile device PreStage enrollment
The ability to supervise devices and require the user to install the MDM Profile during enrollment with a PreStage enrollment will be required and will be built-in functionality. These settings will be removed from the Jamf Pro user interface.
pomManagedClassroomScreenObservation key
This key will be removed from the Restrictions payload for mobile device configuration profiles. It will be replaced with the forceClassroomUnpromptedScreenObservation key.
IfLostReturnToMessage key
The grayscale key will be removed from the Accessibility payload for computer configuration profiles.
Support for non-certificate based client communication with the Jamf Pro server
The Enable certificate-based authentication checkbox will be removed from Settings > Computer Management > Security.

items.title: Resolved Issues — Jamf Pro 11.32.0
items.text:
Note:
Some resolved issues in this release may have been addressed in a previous maintenance release.
Jamf Pro Server: Security Issues
Jamf provides the CVE-ID for security issues with high or critical severity when possible.
[PI17895] Fixed: A sensitive information disclosure issue.
[PI186191] Fixed: A cross-site scripting (XSS) issue.
[PI208395] Fixed: A cross-site scripting (XSS) issue.
[PI209382] Fixed: The Jamf Pro installers include Spring Framework 6.2.18, which includes multiple vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-41842 and CVE-2026-41855.
Jamf Pro Server
[PI-1332] Fixed: When an existing device is re-enrolled using Automated Device Enrollment or user-initiated enrollment, Jamf Pro updates every device linked to that device's user and recalculates smart group membership before responding to the enrollment request. The extra processing can exceed the 60-second enrollment timeout, causing the device to display an "Enrolling with management server failed" error during Setup Assistant.
[PI110307] Fixed: The Jamf Pro interface does not display a New button to create a webhook for some Jamf Pro accounts, even if those accounts have the proper privileges.
[PI148391] Fixed: After modifying the custom configuration PLIST for iOS shared device compliance, Jamf Pro fails to redistribute the updated configuration to target devices until they are re-enrolled.
Note:
This issue was resolved in Jamf Pro 11.31.0 and was inadvertently omitted from those release notes.
[PI173119] [PI173120] Fixed: The Jamf Pro server may experience performance issues when sending MDM commands containing a large binary payload, such as a wallpaper image.
[PI200840] Fixed: Upgrading to Jamf Pro 11.27.0 through 11.31.x deletes Automated Device Enrollment account details for instances that share an MDM server in Apple Business or Apple School Manager.
